text:
rahul: Heads-up — nightly CI reported a latency regression for the small-llm profile. Alerted by the bench job around 03:20 UTC. Not huge, but consistent across three runs :thinking_face:

ops-bot: [alert] perf/nightly/latency breached threshold for model=small-llm, p95 +18% vs baseline. run_id=nightly-2025-10-11-03

maria: Can you paste the benchmark config and whether this was synthetic traffic or replay harness?

rahul: It was the synthetic load generator (continuous-arrival). Config below:
```
model: small-llm
seq: 512
clients: 40
arrival: poisson
batching: continuous
batch_max_tokens: 4096
kv_cache: enabled (cold start)
kernel_selector: auto
```

jen: I ran a quick profile on a repro VM. Kernel selection switched to matmul_opt_v2 at runtime which increased kernel launch overhead for this size. Traces: matmul_opt_v2 selected for seq=512, batch_tokens=3200, decision time ~2.1ms per request.

leo: That's interesting — matmul_opt_v2 has better throughput but higher per-launch latency. For small bursts the old matmul_basic is better. We should compare with kernel_override to get apples-to-apples.

maria: Agreed. Also KV behavior matters: synthetic run started cold; KV warmup during replay gives very different p95. We should test both cold and warm cache.

rahul: Plan: 1) run replay harness (real user traces) with kernel_override=matmul_basic and kernel_override=matmul_opt_v2; 2) run synthetic tests with kv-mode={cold,warm}; 3) capture perf counters and kernel-selection logs; 4) push results to dashboard.

bench-bot: queued job: replay-compare-1751123456 (tags: replay, kernel-override, kv-warm-cold). Link: https://bench.redwood/compare/1751123456

jen: Quick profiling snippet (sample):
```
[profile] op=matmul_opt_v2 latency=0.78ms kernel_launch=1.9ms compute=0.35ms
[profile] op=matmul_basic latency=0.62ms kernel_launch=0.6ms compute=0.3ms
cache: kv_hits=210/300 (warm) vs 12/300 (cold)
```

leo: Those kernel_launch numbers explain the p95 shift. For our CI apples-to-apples, we should: - force kernel_override in CI compare jobs; - fix batch_max_tokens distribution to match production (current synthetic uses higher variance); - add kv-warm prefill step for warm-case runs.

maria: Also suggest adding histograms to the dashboard for kernel selection frequency and per-kernel launch time. That will help triage flakiness instead of a single p95 number.

rahul: For flaky test triage: if nightly shows >12% regression but kernel selection variance explains >60% of regression, mark as flaky and auto-schedule an immediate replay run with kernel_override. We can also temporarily relax thresholds for synthetic-only diffs.

ops-bot: Created incident-annot: perf-nightly-1751123456 with tags [flaky, kernel-selection].

jen: I'll add a small CI step that runs the replay harness (5m sample) and posts side-by-side p95 numbers. If they diverge >8%, fail and attach the profiler output.

leo: One more: batching heuristics. Continuous batching currently uses a 5ms accumulation window. For small-llm that pushes some requests into the slower kernel. Try reducing to 3ms in synthetic to mimic production tail.

maria: Sounds good. After the runs, put the results in the perf dashboard and link the raw traces. If we still see regression after kernel override + kv warm, we'll dig deeper into memory placement and thread pinning.

rahul: Thanks — I'll run the queued jobs and post results here. :thumbsup:
